verdict.line: You lose this if you walk into Mini Gnar's poke range with no plan; you win it by forcing the all-in while his E (Hop) is down.

brief.thesis: Sett has no ranged answer to Mini Gnar's Q (Boomerang Throw) and auto-attack poke, so the entire lane is about denying Gnar space to kite until you can force a fight on your terms. The data backs this up as genuinely even — 48.1% over 2137 games — with the solo-kill edge sitting on your side, meaning Gnar's poke rarely kills you outright but your all-ins land hard when they connect.

theirWindow.when: Mini Gnar, E (Hop) available, at range
theirWindow.what: You have no gap closer, so don't chase — Hop lets him reposition and keep poking with Q and ranged autos while you eat free damage.

yourWindow.what: Hop's cooldown (22/19.5/17/14.5/12s) is his only escape. The moment it's down, close the gap and commit Q (Knuckle Down) into your full combo before he can reset it.

start.why: Sustains through the ranged poke OP.GG flags as the matchup's main threat — it's the top pick at 64.5% for a reason.

boots.why: Cuts down the chip damage from Gnar's auto-attacks stacking up while you close distance.

core.why: The slow-on-hit and burst of movement speed is your only real way to close on a champion who otherwise kites you freely.
Armor shred plus stacking move speed lets you actually catch Mini Gnar before Hop comes back up.
Health and omnivamp to outlast poke and stay alive through Mega Gnar all-ins — pairs with your passive's missing-health regen.

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks through the prolonged poke exchanges this lane forces, converting to healing so you can actually survive long enough to land your combo.

summoners.why: Ignite seals kills on squishy Mini Gnar before he can transform, matching your solo-kill edge; Flash+Ghost (50.3%, 22.6% pick) is the alternative if you'd rather close gaps than secure kills.

playing.title: Wall-stun with minions
playing.detail: E (Facebreaker) only stuns when enemies are pulled from opposite sides of you — against a lone Gnar it just slows him. Line up so a minion sits on his far side before you pull.

playing.title: Trade when Hop is down
playing.detail: The instant Gnar uses E (Hop, cooldown 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s) to poke or reposition, walk up and commit your Q (Knuckle Down) plus autos while he has no escape.

playing.title: Bank Grit before engaging
playing.detail: W (Haymaker) only pays off from stored Grit — take a few hits first instead of opening with it cold, then cash in the shield and punch together.

playing.title: Ult through the kite
playing.detail: R (The Show Stopper) carries Gnar through the air regardless of Hop, so use it to lock down a kiting Mini Gnar instead of chasing autos.

playing.title: Respect the Rage bar late
playing.detail: Once Gnar can transform, his W becomes an area stun and his R a wall-stun knockback — don't commit E or R into him near walls from level 11 on.

playing.title: Let Conqueror win the attrition
playing.detail: Lean on Conqueror's healing to survive the poke phase; Gnar's ranged autos shouldn't out-sustain you before your combo lands.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and win-rate figures are pulled from measured games on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade-timing calls are my own read on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Keep your distance to avoid being kited by Gnar. Keep Mega Gnar’s (R) in mind while fighting him.
